s01_title: Git assumes the person who wrote a change is expensive to ask twice. That is why branches live long, conflicts are merged by hand, and review means a human reading a diff. Agents break that assumption: redoing work costs pennies. Braid is version control built on that fact.
s02_ideas: Four ideas. A change is an intent: a goal, a declared scope of files, and an acceptance note. The diff is just the current attempt. Every attempt gets its own strand: a real Artifacts fork with its own tokens and its own rate limit. The lease is the token: claiming a change mints a write token whose lifetime is the lease. And conflicts are replayed, never merged by hand.
s03_spawn: This is the dashboard. On the right, a conference website that lives in an Artifacts repo called trunk. On the left, a backlog of changes. Let's spawn eight Workers AI agents. Each agent claims a change, which forks trunk into a private strand and mints a write token whose lifetime is the lease. The agent clones, edits only inside its scope, pushes, and submits. The Integrator is the only writer to trunk. It diffs each strand without cloning, using readCommit and readTree, checks the scope, asks a reviewer whether the diff does what the intent says, three-way merges, and pushes once per weave. Watch the site update as changes land. Several changes touched site dot json at the same time: the manifest got a structural union merge. And held back is claims mode: overlapping scopes wait their turn.
s04_conflict: Now optimistic mode. Two agents rewrite the same headline. The first one lands. The second one conflicts. Braid never writes merge markers. The change goes back to an agent with a hint, and is replayed on the new trunk. Two attempts, one clean commit, and the full history of both.
s05_mcp: Any coding agent can join with one line. Claude Code asks Braid for a change over MCP, gets a strand and a lease token, and uses plain git. Braid treats it exactly like its own agents: scope check, review, weave.
s06_revoke: The lease is enforced by Artifacts, not by convention. Revoke an agent, and its next push is a 403. Its change goes back to the pool.
s07_swarm: A thousand agents. Each one a real Artifacts fork, a real clone, and a real push with its own lease token, all editing the same file. Union merges land them a few hundred a minute, one trunk push per weave. The same design shards to a hundred thousand: a coordinator per scope prefix, a namespace per shard, and a tree of integrators feeding trunk. Many strands, one rope.
s08_code: Every line on trunk knows why it exists. Browse any ref straight from Artifacts, with no clone. Ask why a file looks the way it does. Open a commit: the diff, the agent, the model, the reviewer's verdict, the replay chain, and a git note with the full context. Clone it anywhere, and the story comes along.
s09_arch: Under the hood: a Worker routed with Blaze, a Coordinator Durable Object that hands out claims and leases, an Integrator that weaves, one Agent Runner per agent, Workers AI for editing and review, and Artifacts for every repo, every token, and every read.
s10_close: Braid. Agents ship intents, not pull requests. Built on Cloudflare Workers and Artifacts.
